overclaims: Available market studies measure different portions of generative AI spending.
More importantly, spending estimates and evidence of customer value do not show whether every purchase depends on subsidies.
checks.note: The rationale talks about several market studies and about evidence of customer value. Only one evidence item is cited: e4, the Menlo enterprise estimate. The Apollo report and the Stanford paper were considered but not used, so the plural claim and the customer-value claim have no support in the cited evidence. Smaller point: e4's excerpt, "$19 billion", is a bare number with no label. Excerpt, proposition, conditions and the unresolved causal outcome are fine.

The proposition keeps the debt details he gave: $40B, payable in a year, over the 25% limit. e1 backs the short maturity (facility signed 2026-03-27, maturing 2027-03-25) and the facility-versus-drawdown split. e2 backs the credit concerns and shows the LTV breach was a projection. The limitation that the reporting came before the facility is correctly dated (March 5 vs March 27). The unresolved causal outcome matches the reviews. One small mismatch: the e2 page header says 4 March, the dateline says March 5.

The excerpt is verbatim, and the proposition keeps "I wager", "first of a few" and "both". e1 and e2 document IPO preparation at both firms. e3 (April 4) supports one Anthropic tightening and e4 (May 6) the easing. The open-horizon, unresolved outcome matches the reviews. Small issue: the payload never says what "this" refers to (Anthropic's March rate-limit cuts). Also, the condition "as they head toward IPO filings" is a paraphrase, not his words.
